items.stem: A team wants to record why it chose event-driven integration over synchronous calls, including the alternatives it rejected. Which artifact fits?

options.rationale: Correct: an ADR captures context, the decision, the alternatives and the consequences.
A runbook documents operational steps, not design rationale.
A burndown tracks progress, not architectural decisions.
A test report shows test outcomes, not decision rationale.

items.explanation: Correct: ADRs exist to capture a decision together with its context and rejected alternatives.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO elements make a good ADR more useful later? (Select TWO)

options.text: The context and forces that drove the decision
options.rationale: Correct: future readers need the context to judge whether the decision still holds.

options.text: The alternatives considered and why they were rejected
options.rationale: Correct: recorded alternatives let a later team re-evaluate without redoing the analysis.

options.text: The author's job title in large font
options.rationale: Formatting of the author's title adds no decision value.

options.text: A promise never to revisit the decision
options.rationale: ADRs are meant to be superseded, not frozen.

items.explanation: Correct: context and rejected alternatives are what make an ADR valuable to future readers.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source
items.scoring: all-or-nothing on the exact key set

items.stem: In the C4 model, which diagram is most appropriate to show a non-technical stakeholder how the system fits among its users and external systems?

options.rationale: Correct: the context diagram shows the system, its users and external systems at the highest level.
Class diagrams are too detailed for a stakeholder overview.
Component diagrams expose internal structure beyond stakeholder needs.
An ER diagram shows data structure, not the system's place among users.

items.explanation: Correct: the C4 context diagram is the highest-level view intended for a broad audience.
